title: Moving Coil Galvanometer
short_intro: A moving coil galvanometer is an electromechanical measuring instrument used for detecting and indicating small electric currents. It operates on the principle that a current-carrying coil placed in a uniform magnetic field experiences a deflecting torque.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Basic construction, working principle, conversion of galvanometer into ammeter and voltmeter using shunts and multipliers.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Ballistic galvanometer equations, charge sensitivity, damping, logarithmic decrement, and correction for damping in flux measurements.

prerequisites: Magnetic effect of electric current and Lorentz force
Torque on a current loop in a magnetic field
Hooke's law of elasticity and torsional constant of a suspension wire

concept_notes.heading: Principle of Moving Coil Galvanometer
bullets: A current-carrying coil suspended in a uniform magnetic field experiences a magnetic torque.
The deflecting torque is directly proportional to the current flowing through the coil.
Restoring torque is provided by the elastic twist of the suspension wire or a hairspring.

concept_notes.heading: Radial Magnetic Field
bullets: A radial magnetic field is achieved by using a cylindrical soft iron core and concave pole pieces.
In a radial field, the magnetic field lines are always parallel to the plane of the coil for any orientation.
This ensures that the deflecting torque remains independent of the angle of deflection, making the scale linear.

concept_notes.heading: Conversion into Ammeter
bullets: A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting a very low resistance called a shunt in parallel with it.
The shunt bypasses the major portion of the main current, protecting the delicate galvanometer coil.
The effective resistance of the resulting ammeter is extremely small compared to the galvanometer resistance.

concept_notes.heading: Conversion into Voltmeter
bullets: A galvanometer is converted into a voltmeter by connecting a very high resistance in series with it.
The high series resistance limits the current passing through the galvanometer when large potential differences are applied.
The effective resistance of the resulting voltmeter is very large, drawing negligible current from the circuit being measured.

derivations.title: Torque and Deflection in Galvanometer
derivations.conditions: Radial magnetic field, N turns of coil with area A
steps: Let a coil of N turns and area A carry current I in a radial magnetic field B.
The magnetic force on each vertical side of length l is F = NIbB, where b is the breadth and A = l * b.
The deflecting torque is given by tau_d = N I A B.
Equating deflecting torque to restoring torque tau_r = k * theta, where k is the torsional constant and theta is deflection: N I A B = k * theta.

derivations.title: Shunt Resistance for Ammeter Conversion
derivations.conditions: Galvanometer resistance G, full-scale deflection current I_g, maximum range I
steps: Let the maximum current to be measured be I, and the current passing through the galvanometer at full-scale deflection be I_g.
The remaining current (I - I_g) must pass through the parallel shunt resistance S.
Since the galvanometer and shunt are in parallel, the potential difference across them is equal: I_g * G = (I - I_g) * S.
Solving for S yields the required shunt resistance.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Current vs Deflection Graph
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A straight line passing through the origin with deflection theta on the y-axis and current I on the x-axis.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: The slope of the line represents the current sensitivity (NAB / k) of the galvanometer, confirming linearity due to the radial field.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Used to determine current sensitivity and figure of merit experimentally.

solved_numericals.question: A galvanometer has a resistance of 50 ohm and shows full scale deflection for a current of 2 mA. Calculate the value of the shunt resistance required to convert it into an ammeter of range 0 to 5 A.
solution_steps: Identify given values: G = 50 ohm, I_g = 2 mA = 2 * 10^-3 A, I = 5 A.
Apply the shunt formula: S = (I_g * G) / (I - I_g).

solved_numericals.question: A galvanometer has a coil resistance of 30 ohm and gives full-scale deflection for 15 mA. Find the series resistance needed to convert it into a voltmeter reading up to 150 V.
solution_steps: Identify given values: G = 30 ohm, I_g = 15 mA = 15 * 10^-3 A, V = 150 V.
Apply the multiplier formula: R = (V / I_g) - G.

solved_numericals.question: A moving coil galvanometer has 100 turns, each of area 2 cm^2. The magnetic field is 0.2 T, and the torsional constant of the suspension strip is 10^-6 N*m/rad. Find its current sensitivity.
solution_steps: Identify given parameters: N = 100, A = 2 cm^2 = 2 * 10^-4 m^2, B = 0.2 T, k = 10^-6 N*m/rad.
Formula for current sensitivity: S_i = (N * A * B) / k.

assumptions_and_limitations: The magnetic field in the gap is assumed to be strictly radial to maintain a linear scale, which holds true only for carefully shaped pole pieces and small deflections.
The restoring torque is assumed to follow Hooke's torsional law linearly, which fails if the elastic limit of the suspension wire is exceeded.

common_misconceptions.wrong: An ideal galvanometer has zero resistance.
common_misconceptions.correct: A practical galvanometer has a definite finite coil resistance (G).
common_misconceptions.why: The coil is made of fine insulated copper wire which inherently possesses electrical resistance.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Connecting a shunt increases the current measuring capacity by blocking all current from the galvanometer.
common_misconceptions.correct: The galvanometer still carries its full-scale current I_g while the shunt carries the excess current (I - I_g).
common_misconceptions.why: Current divides inversely proportional to resistances in a parallel network.

quick_revision: Radial magnetic field ensures linear deflection scale: theta is proportional to I.
Ammeter uses a small parallel shunt; Voltmeter uses a large series multiplier.
